text.p: The company did not provide comparative 1995 figures for its fourth-quarter results, but in a press statement said net earnings for the period rose 462 percent to $5 million.
It attributed most of the quarterly rise to a one-time gain from its Agan Chemical Manufacturers unit of $4 million arising from a court settlement.

Gross margins at Makhteshim, a maker of agrochemicals, fell for the year to 28.4 percent from 29.5 percent in 1995, but the company indicated they grew in the final quarter. Operating margins edged up to 11.4 percent for the year from 11.1 percent.

"The year 1996 constituted a turning point for the operations of the Makhteshim Group, which was brought about by ensuring (international) marketing channels...through the acquisition of marketing and manfacturing companies and by signing multi-year contracts...with multinational companies," managing director Shlomo Yonas said in a statement.
Makhteshim said sales to Latin America rose 52 percent in the year to $109.3 million. It said the regional companies it acquired contributed $32.7 million of the total.
